result: The authors identify separation-of-function mutations in the TEN-domain of hTERT (K78E, R132E, and K78E;R132E) that disrupt RAP stimulation by POT1-TPP1 in vitro while retaining substantial catalytic activity (63-92% of wild-type).
evaluation: Reviewers raised significant concerns about the quantification methods and interpretation of activity data. They noted discrepancies between Figure 1 and Figure 4B activity measurements, questioned the normalization methods, and challenged the claim that these residues are 'not essential for enzyme activity' when the double mutant shows only 63% activity. Reviewers requested better description of quantification methods and raw data before normalization.

result: The authors conclude that RAP stimulation defects in K78E and R132E mutants are due to failure of telomerase to interact with TPP1, and that these mutants fail to localize to telomeres in vivo due to this interaction defect rather than an activity defect.
evaluation: Reviewers fundamentally challenged this conclusion, stating that 'all of the evidence presented here is in vivo and thus no clear conclusion about any possible bridging protein can be made.' They emphasized that without direct biochemical demonstration of protein-protein interaction, the conclusion of direct interaction is not supported. Reviewers requested biochemical assays (Biacore, GST pull-downs, etc.) to demonstrate direct interaction.

result: The authors show by immunofluorescence that wild-type telomerase localizes to telomeres and forms neo-Cajal bodies, while TEN-domain mutants (K78E, R132E, K78E;R132E) localize only to Cajal bodies and not to telomeres, indicating that telomerase assembly is unaffected by TEN-domain mutations.
evaluation: Reviewers raised major concerns about the overexpression approach used in these experiments, noting that 'overexpression of proteins is known to cause spurious cellular localization' and that the different patterns may simply indicate that 'mutants may aggregate differently in the cell.' They stated that overexpression experiments are 'not sufficient to conclude the proteins fail to localize to telomeres' and requested alternative methods without overexpression (ChIP, Co-IP) to validate localization conclusions.

result: The authors demonstrate that expression of wild-type hTERT causes progressive telomere elongation to ~14.8 kb, while TEN-domain mutants K78E and R132E fail to elongate telomeres despite having higher telomerase activity per cell than parental HeLa cells.
evaluation: Reviewers questioned whether the failure to elongate telomeres is due to recruitment defects or reduced intrinsic activity. They noted that 'given that the mutants K78E and R132E showed decreased telomerase enzyme activity in the experiments in Figure 1, it is not surprising that there is less telomere elongation.' Reviewers were concerned that overexpression of mutant enzymes with decreased activity would 'sequester all of the hTR and result in overall reduced telomerase activity.' In later rounds, reviewers stated the evidence is 'not sufficient to say that telomeres shrink' due to telomere heterogeneity.

result: The authors demonstrate charge-swap rescue: TPP1 E215K fully rescues the RAP stimulation defect of hTERT K78E (from 68% to 98%), while non-cognate combinations show reduced stimulation, suggesting direct interaction between K78 on hTERT TEN-domain and E215 on TPP1 TEL-patch.
evaluation: Reviewers found the charge-swap data compelling, stating 'the direct assay data for the hTERT K78E TPP1 E215K combination is compelling.' In their rebuttal evaluation, reviewers acknowledged that 'the authors are persuasive in the rebuttal that the PT stimulation is an excellent proxy for direct protein-protein interaction' and that 'the charge-swap mutants provide such a strong argument for a direct protein-protein interaction.' However, they noted that R132E does not show much compensation, questioning why it is still shown in the model.

result: Using a LacI tethering assay, the authors show that wild-type telomerase co-localizes with TPP1-OB-fold domain in ~90% of nuclei, while TEN-domain mutants show reduced co-localization (55%, 30%, 0% for K78E, R132E, K78E;R132E respectively). The E215K mutation in TPP1 significantly increases co-localization of K78E telomerase, demonstrating compensatory rescue in vivo.
evaluation: Reviewers raised significant concerns about the LacI assay data, noting 'the variability of the number mCh-hTERT dots in the nucleus' is 'very confusing' and that 'these experiments are very difficult to interpret.' They questioned whether the quantitation was done in a blinded fashion and requested that 'best practice for this kind of experiment is to have the person scoring the localization blind to the genotype.' Reviewers also noted that 'since this is an in vivo assay, if there were a bridging protein it would still be present, so the main conclusion about a charged interaction being the main interaction cannot be concluded from this experiment.'

result: The authors show that expression of E215K TPP1 in cells expressing K78E hTERT triggers telomere length increase to ~7.7 kb over 6 weeks, rescuing telomere length maintenance by driving telomerase recruitment to telomeres.
evaluation: Reviewers did not raise specific concerns about this telomere length rescue experiment in the final rounds of review. The data appears to have been accepted as supporting the charge-swap rescue model, though reviewers had earlier concerns about telomere length heterogeneity and requested multiple independent clones to demonstrate reproducibility.

result: The authors show that the disease-associated mutation V144M retains 48% activity and 95% processivity but shows reduced RAP stimulation (61% of wild-type). TEL-patch mutants E169K and E215K show additive loss of RAP stimulation with V144M (28% and 37% respectively), indicating V144M and E215K affect separate components of the telomerase-TPP1 interface.
evaluation: Reviewers initially stated that 'this figure does not contribute in any way to the point of this paper' and that 'the addition of this mutant onto the end of this paper is distracting and does not belong here.' They recommended removing this data and publishing it in another study. While the data was apparently retained in later versions, the reviewers' initial assessment suggests this was considered tangential to the main findings.

result: The authors conclude that K78 and R132 within the TEN-domain of hTERT mediate direct interaction with the TEL-patch of TPP1 to recruit telomerase to telomeres, and that this direct TEN-domain-TEL-patch interaction is necessary and may be sufficient for telomerase recruitment in humans.
evaluation: Reviewers fundamentally challenged the conclusion of 'direct interaction,' stating that 'without any direct demonstration of an interaction of TPP1 and the TEN domain that is mediated by the charge swap mutants that are described, the conclusions here are not supported by the data.' They emphasized that 'all of the evidence presented here is in vivo and thus no clear conclusion about any possible bridging protein can be made.' While reviewers later acknowledged the charge-swap data as persuasive evidence for direct interaction, they maintained concerns about the strength of the overall conclusion without biochemical validation.
